# How to Turn a Job Description Into a Resume Checklist With AI

> **In short:** Paste a job posting into any AI assistant, ask it to list the skills, keywords and experience the employer wants, then check each item against your own resume. The AI's list is a starting point you verify yourself, not a promise of interviews.

By the end of this guide, you will be able to take any job posting, have an AI assistant sort it into a clear checklist, and compare that checklist with your resume so you can see what already matches and what is missing. This is useful if you are changing jobs, returning to work, or just want your resume to speak the employer's language. You do not need any technical background.

## Before you start

- **An AI assistant account.** Any popular AI chatbot works for this. Many offer a free version, and some features may need a paid plan, but this task usually runs fine on the free level.
- **A job posting.** Open one from a job website or an email and keep it ready to copy.
- **Your current resume** in a document or text file you can open and copy from.
- **About 20 to 30 minutes** for your first run.

## Step 1 — Copy the job posting text

Open the job posting in your browser. Click at the very start of the description, hold the mouse button (or press and hold on your phone's screen), and drag down to the end so the whole text is highlighted. Then copy it using Ctrl+C on a Windows computer or Command+C on a Mac, or choose "Copy" from the menu that appears on a phone.

Skip the company logo and the "apply now" buttons. You only want the words that describe the job. If the posting is split into sections like "About us" and "What you'll do," include all of them, because the requirements are often hidden in the later sections.

If the copy picks up a lot of menu text from the website, that's fine, the AI can ignore it. If you can't select the text at all, look for a "print" or "share" option on the page and copy from there instead.

You'll know it worked when you have the posting text on your clipboard and you can paste it into a plain text document and read the job duties and requirements.

## Step 2 — Open an AI assistant and start a new chat

Open the AI assistant app or website you use. Look for a button like "New chat" or a pencil icon that starts a fresh conversation. Starting fresh keeps your job search separate from anything else you've asked before.

Find the message box, which is usually a text box near the bottom of the screen. Tap or click inside it so the cursor blinks there. On a phone, the keyboard will slide up. On a computer, you can start typing right away.

If you don't see a "new chat" button, look for a plus sign or a menu with three dots and choose the option to start a new conversation. If you're already in a chat that's empty, you can use it.

Paste the job posting into the message box now, using Ctrl+V or Command+V, or the paste option on your phone. You will usually see the long text appear in the box. Don't send it yet, because the next step tells the AI what to do with it.

You'll know it worked when the full job posting is sitting in the message box and you can scroll through it.

## Step 3 — Ask for a checklist of requirements

With the job posting still in the box, type your instructions above or below it. Add your request in the same message so the AI knows what to do. Keep your words plain and specific. The AI works best when you tell it the format you want.

💬 Example: "Below is a job posting for a [job title] role. List the required skills, tools and experience it asks for. Split the list into must-haves and nice-to-haves, and keep the employer's exact wording for each item so I can match my resume to it."

Then press the send button, usually an arrow or paper-airplane icon next to the message box, or press Enter on a computer. The AI will read the posting and write its answer in the chat below your message. This can take anywhere from a few seconds to a minute.

If the answer is too general, reply with "Please list each item as a short phrase, with no paragraphs." If it misses something obvious, ask it to look again at a specific section. The AI can misread a posting or leave things out, so treat its list as a draft.

You'll know it worked when the reply shows two clear groups, must-haves and nice-to-haves, each made up of short items.

## Step 4 — Save the checklist in a document

Copy the AI's answer so you can keep it. Select the text in the reply, then copy it the same way you copied the job posting. Open a note, a word processor, or a notes app on your phone, and paste the list there.

Give the document a clear name, such as "Checklist - [job title] - [company name]." Including the company name matters, because you will probably apply to several jobs and the lists will look alike.

Read through the items and delete anything that doesn't make sense or that you can see is just filler from the posting, like "great communication skills" written generically. Keep items that name a specific tool, a certification, a task, or a number of years of experience. Those are the things a hiring manager is most likely to look for, and they are the easiest to check.

If the AI's answer is hard to read, ask it in the chat to reformat the list as a plain bulleted list with no extra commentary, then copy that version instead.

You'll know it worked when you have a saved document with a short, clean list of items you can tick off one at a time.

## Step 5 — Check your resume against the list

Open your current resume next to the checklist. For each item, ask yourself: "Do I have real experience with this, and does my resume say so?" Mark each one as "shows it," "have it but not written down," or "missing." Being honest here helps you more than being generous.

Once you've marked your own copy, you can use the AI to double-check. Start a new chat or use the same one, paste your resume text, and ask it to compare. This step is useful because it's easy to overlook a skill you mentioned in a different way.

💬 Example: "Here is my current resume: [paste your resume here]. For each item on my checklist, tell me whether my resume clearly shows it, and quote the line that does. If it doesn't show it, say so plainly."

If the AI says a skill is missing when you know you have it, check the wording. The resume may use a different name for the same thing, such as "customer complaints" instead of "customer service." Your own judgment should win, because you know your work history best.

You'll know it worked when every item on your checklist has a clear mark next to it, and you know which ones you can prove and which ones you need to address.

## Step 6 — Update your resume honestly

Now look at the items you marked "have it but not written down." These are your best opportunities. Rewrite the relevant bullet point so it uses the job's words, but only if the sentence describes work you actually did. Do not add skills or tools you have never used, and do not claim years of experience you don't have. A resume that is honest is more useful than one that is impressive on paper and falls apart in an interview.

If a requirement is truly missing, you have three honest choices: leave it out, mention related experience, or decide the job isn't a good fit. You can also consider a short course to learn it, but that's your decision to make, and this checklist can't tell you whether to apply.

Use the AI as a wording helper, not a writer of your history. Paste one line at a time and ask it to rephrase, then read each result and change anything that isn't true.

💬 Example: "Help me reword this resume line so it uses the job's language, but only describes work I actually did: [paste one resume line here]."

You'll know it worked when each updated line is something you could explain confidently in an interview.

## Common mistakes

- **Trusting the list without reading the posting.** The AI can misread or skip details. Fix this by spot-checking the list against the original posting, especially the "requirements" section.
- **Copying the AI's wording straight into your resume.** Keyword stuffing can read as robotic, and it can claim skills you don't have. Fix this by rewriting each line in your own voice and keeping only what's true.
- **Using one resume for every job.** A single version rarely matches every posting well. Fix this by saving a separate checklist and a tailored version for each job you seriously want.

## What this means for you

- **In everyday life:** Use this method to understand a job you're thinking about, such as a part-time shift or a career change, before you spend time on applications.
- **For your business or work:** If you hire or manage a team, you can use the same approach to write clearer job postings and check which skills really matter.
- **If you're just getting started:** Start with a single job posting you already like. Finishing one checklist teaches you more than reading about the method.

One honest limit: the AI can organize the posting and compare it with your resume, but it cannot know what a specific employer will actually value, and it cannot submit or track your applications for you.

## Try it now

Pick one job posting you're curious about, copy its text, and paste it into your AI assistant with this request: "List the must-have skills and experience in this job posting as a short bulleted list, using the employer's own words." You'll have a usable checklist in about two minutes.
